newsitem.title: USA: U.S. urges Iran to annul Bahai death sentences.
newsitem.headline: U.S. urges Iran to annul Bahai death sentences.

text.p: The United States on Friday condemned a decision by Iran's supreme court to uphold death sentences on two members of the Bahai faith and called on Iran to release the men.

The U.S. State Department said the Iranian court had upheld sentences passed on Musa Talibi and Zabihullah Mahrami, who were convicted separately last year of "apostasy," a term used in Iran to denote abandoning Islam.
"The United States government strongly condemns this action and calls on the government of Iran to release these men," spokesman Nicholas Burns said in a statement.
"We urge the government of Iran to free all prisoners of conscience and to ensure freedom of religion and other basic human rights in Iran," he said.
The United States had already appealed on behalf of both men when their original sentences were passed.

The Bahai faith, an offshoot of Islam, was created in Iran 150 years ago. It claims six million members worldwide including 350,000 in Iran where it is officially considered "a misleading and wayward sect."
Bahais in the United States say more than 200 members of their faith have been executed in Iran for their religious beliefs since the Islamic revolution in 1979.
